nodes.tagline: Monitoring and learning layer for long-running agents
nodes.description:
BentoLabs is the monitoring and learning layer for long-running agents. We detect when agents silently fail or drift from the user's goal, system prompt, or tool contracts, show affected users and root cause, and suggest the prompt, skill, or harness fix.

As more teams deploy agents, keeping them reliable in production becomes mission-critical. Bento sits directly in the production loop and gives teams the operational leverage required to scale agent ecosystems without scaling human firefighting alongside them. The result is a system that turns opaque agents into agents that can be monitored, debugged, and improved continuously.

The founders learned this problem at Emergent (YC S24), where they built and operated production coding agents used by 5M+ users. Abhinav was hire #1 and helped Emergent hit SWE-Bench #1 and scale from $0 to $100M ARR in just 8 months. Kaushik was hire #2, led full-stack engineering at Emergent, and was key to building the infrastructure that made production agents reliable, observable, and debuggable. Bento's self-learning engine has also lifted ARC-AGI-3 (internal) by 2.6x and Terminal-Bench 2.0 (internal) from 42.2% to 52.4% pass@1 with the same model, tools, and budget.

nodes.description:
Foaster is building the AI-native McKinsey, starting with AI transformation.

We deploy AI agents that interview a company's employees at scale, map how work actually gets done, identify bottlenecks and AI opportunities, and draft a transformation roadmap in just 2 weeks. Expert consultants review the final outputs, add judgment where it matters, and feed their corrections back into the system.

We are starting with AI transformation, then progressively expanding to more and more consulting projects using the same approach. The $500B consulting market will eventually be run by our AI agents and a small number of expert humans.

nodes.description:
Klaimee is the first insurance for your AI agents. It covers what traditional E&O and cyber explicitly carve out, so you can deploy agentic AI at scale with real peace of mind.

The problem: AI agents are taking actions autonomously buying, emailing, modifying sensitive data. AB 316 already holds deployers liable. EU AI Act enforces in August. Enterprise legal asks "who pays if your agent breaks something?" and there's no good answer.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
We built the answer. Critical-category risk evaluation, certification, financial guarantee, liability insurance and the documentation enterprise procurement needs to sign off.

We understand how insurance works, what enterprises require, and why startups can't wait 6 months for either.

nodes.description:
Sentry and Datadog dump a stream of alerts. Most are duplicates, most lack context, and you still have to solve the issue yourself.

Superlog is AI-native observability that's meant not to be opened. A wizard scans your repo and installs proper OpenTelemetry instrumentation, then runs daily to keep up as you ship new code. When something breaks, Superlog groups the errors into a single incident, investigates with full context (logs, traces, recent deploys, past Slack threads), and posts one mergeable PR in Slack. You merge it, ignore it, or open it as a Claude Code session and modify it.

Telemetry is vendor-neutral, so you keep every log, trace, and metric we install, even if you leave.

biggestContribution.text:
🎉 New Investment: InsForge 🎉
I'm excited to share that I'm investing in InsForge alongside Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund.
InsForge is the backend platform built for AI-native development. Backend tools today assume a human at every step, with dashboards and manual configs. As coding agents become the primary builders, that model breaks down. InsForge gives an agent one consistent CLI to deploy and operate the full backend: servers, database, auth, and storage. Every primitive returns structured outputs and readable errors, while branching, scoped permissions, and reversible writes keep changes safe to review or discard. An agent can build, run, debug, and scale an app end to end.
Hang Huang and Tony (Yaowen) Chang are a strong fit for this. Hang, the CEO, is a former Amazon product manager and former pro League of Legends player. Tony, the CTO, was a network infrastructure engineer at Databricks. Together they pair deep infrastructure depth with the conviction that coding agents will soon run entire applications on their own.

He previously worked in reactor operations at Engie and an advanced reactor designer with EDF, the world's largest nuclear operator. Co-founder and COO Drew Walker previously co-founded Blue Innovations Group, an electric boat startup, and served in the White House. Deep nuclear engineering credibility paired with commercial and operations execution. Exactly the team this industry needs.
Let's goo!

▫️ Thomas — the first YC-backed AI founder. A virtual human that starts, runs, and grows its own companies. Not a tool for founders; the founder itself.
▫️ Humwork (YC P26) — connects stuck agents to verified human experts in under 30 seconds via MCP. Waymo's remote driver assistance, but for agents.
▫️ RentAHuman — a marketplace where AI agents hire humans for physical, regulatory, or judgment-heavy tasks.
▫️ AgentPhone — gives every agent its own phone number with voice and messaging through one API. Already used by teams at Google's ADK, Replit, Y Combinator, and LangChain.
▫️ Chronicle Labs — staging environments for enterprise agents. Captures every production event and backtests new behaviors before deployment.
▫️ InsForge — agent-native cloud infrastructure. Coding agents deploy and operate the entire backend from a single CLI.
▫️ Klaimee (YC P26) — the first purpose-built E&O coverage for AI agents, just as Berkshire, Chubb, and Travelers win approval to exclude AI liability from standard policies.
▫️ Mount — a full AI insurance carrier, starting with liability coverage for deployed agents. Two companies attacking this gap in one batch is itself a signal.
▫️ Primitive — the communication layer for agents to coordinate, hand off tasks, and share context.
▫️ Standout (YC P26) — a hiring marketplace where autonomous agents represent both candidates and companies.
▫️ Superset — the IDE for running hundreds of coding agents in parallel.
